content.value_statement: Systems biology teams need reliable guidance for COBRApy analyses, from model loading to flux studies. This skill provides focused workflows and API patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to load, save, and inspect SBML, JSON, and YAML metabolic models.
Guides flux balance analysis, parsimonious FBA, geometric FBA, and flux variability analysis.
Supports gene deletion, reaction deletion, knockout screens, and growth impact interpretation.
Covers media changes, minimal media calculations, production envelopes, and gapfilling workflows.
Documents model validation, mass balance checks, flux sampling, and common COBRApy object patterns.
limitations: Does not install COBRApy, solvers, or external model files for the user.
Requires valid metabolic models and solver support for accurate numerical results.
Cannot guarantee biological correctness without experimental context and expert review.
Large genome-scale analyses may require more compute than an interactive session provides.

use_cases.title: Run Baseline Metabolic Simulations
use_cases.description: Load a model, check feasibility, run FBA, and interpret growth and flux outputs.

use_cases.title: Screen Engineering Targets
use_cases.description: Evaluate gene or reaction knockouts and compare effects on growth or product formation.

use_cases.title: Teach COBRApy Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn core COBRApy APIs into clear examples for model structure, constraints, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Load and Inspect a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cobrapy skill to explain how to load the textbook model, inspect reactions, metabolites, and genes, and check growth feasibility.

prompt_templates.title: Plan FBA and FVA
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cobrapy skill to plan flux balance analysis and flux variability analysis for my SBML model. Include validation steps and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Knockout Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cobrapy skill to design a gene knockout screen that identifies essential genes, neutral genes, and growth effects. Include practical thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Production Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cobrapy skill to compare production envelopes, media constraints, FVA, and knockout combinations for a target metabolite. Explain tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: I need to find essential genes in an E. coli model.
output_examples.output: A structured workflow for loading the model, running baseline growth, applying single gene deletion, filtering growth results, and interpreting essentiality.

output_examples.input: My model is feasible, but several fluxes have wide ranges.
output_examples.output: A diagnostic plan using FVA, loopless FVA, flux sampling, and reaction-specific plots to explain uncertainty and alternate pathways.

output_examples.input: I want to improve acetate production while preserving growth.
output_examples.output: A production analysis plan covering target objective setup, minimum growth constraints, production envelopes, candidate knockouts, and result interpretation.

best_practices: Validate model feasibility before running expensive analyses or comparing biological scenarios.
Use context managers for temporary objective, medium, bound, or knockout changes.
Check solver status and numerical stability before interpreting growth or flux values.
anti_patterns: Do not compare knockout results against an undefined or stale baseline growth value.
Do not modify reaction bounds without recording the biological assumption behind each constraint.
Do not treat computational predictions as experimental evidence without domain review.

faq.question: What is COBRApy used for?
faq.answer: COBRApy supports constraint-based analysis of metabolic models, including growth prediction, flux studies, knockouts, and model validation.

faq.question: Can this skill analyze SBML models?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to load, save, validate, and analyze SBML models through COBRApy workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill run solvers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user environment must provide COBRApy, compatible solvers, and model files.

faq.question: Can it help with gene knockout studies?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers single and double deletion workflows, essential gene filtering, and growth impact interpretation.

faq.question: Does it support metabolic engineering tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes production envelopes, media constraints, gapfilling, and knockout strategy guidance for target metabolites.

faq.question: What should users verify before trusting results?
faq.answer: Users should verify model quality, solver status, objective choice, constraints, biological assumptions, and experimental relevance.
